purpose: Execution of chapter 2 of the UNIDROIT Principles of International Commercial Contracts (2016 edition): formation of the contract (section 1, art. 2.1.1–2.1.22) and authority of agents (section 2, art. 2.2.1–2.2.10). The types for party, contract, term, notice and the organ of evaluative elements come from the hub `unidroit.picc`. This package is where the substantive difference from the 1980 UN Convention becomes observable: a knock-out rule against the two readings of article 19, a period for acceptance running from the dispatch of the offer, pre-contractual liability and agency, none of which the Convention has. The list of questions and boundaries is in analysis/questions.json and QUESTIONS.md.
limitations: THIS IS NOT THE LAW OF A STATE. The Principles apply when the parties have agreed on them, or when a court or arbitral tribunal takes them as general principles of law; they do not replace the mandatory rules of the applicable law (article 1.4, hub `unidroit.picc`).

THE EVALUATIVE ELEMENTS OF CHAPTER 2 GO THROUGH THE §47.3 JUDGMENT CHANNEL with the organ `Tribunal`: material alteration of an offer or a contract (2.1.11, 2.1.12), reasonable reliance on the irrevocability of an offer (2.1.4), a reasonable time for acceptance and for notice (2.1.7, 2.1.9), bad faith in negotiations (2.1.15), whether a standard term is one the other party could reasonably have expected (2.1.20), a reasonable belief of the third party caused by the principal (2.2.5(2)), the unreasonableness of expecting the agent to act personally (2.2.8). The model neither decides them nor substitutes a guess.

THE DIFFERENCE FROM THE CONVENTION IS WRITTEN AS RULES, NOT AS A COMMENT. The Principles settle the "battle of forms" by a knock-out rule (article 2.1.22): the contract is concluded on the terms agreed and on the standard terms that are common in substance. Article 19 of the Convention has no such rule, and its two §152 readings live in `intl.uncitral.cisg_formation`. The period for acceptance runs from the DISPATCH of the offer (article 2.1.8), not from its delivery. On the same facts the two instruments answer differently, and this is observed by cases 02 and 01 rather than asserted.

PRE-CONTRACTUAL LIABILITY, STANDARD TERMS AND AGENCY ARE ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE CONVENTION: articles 2.1.15–2.1.22 and 2.2.1–2.2.10 have no bridge to `intl.uncitral.cisg*` in substance, not for want of work.

THE INTERNAL RELATIONSHIP OF AGENCY IS NOT FORMALISED: section 2.2 itself declares (article 2.2.1(2)) that it governs only the external relations of the agent with the third party; the relations between agent and principal are left to the applicable law and to the case.

AUTHORITY GRANTED BY LAW AND REPRESENTATION BY AN ORGAN OF A LEGAL ENTITY ARE EXCLUDED BY THE SOURCE ITSELF (article 2.2.1(3)): their conditions are a question of the applicable law, not of the Principles.

THE PRINCIPLES HAVE NO CALENDAR: which days are non-business days at the offeror's place of business is a fact of the case. The §86 policy of the package counts calendar days, and the extension for a holiday is expressed by a rule of the hub over the facts of the case.
